repos.description: An Anthropic-managed, curated directory of Claude Code plugins.
repos.analysis: Anthropic's official plugin marketplace for Claude Code, hosting pre-built slash commands, agents, skills, and MCP server configurations in a curated, quality-reviewed registry. It trended as the authoritative hub for Claude Code extensibility — developers now have a single trusted source to discover and install community and partner plugins. Claude Code users who want to supercharge their workflow without building integrations from scratch will benefit most, and plugin authors gain a credentialed publishing platform.
repos.llm_api_note: Plugin directory for Claude Code; Claude subscription or API key required

repos.description: A self-hosted AI job-search framework built on Claude Code for evaluating postings, tailoring CVs, drafting cover letters, and preparing for interviews.
repos.analysis: An open-source, self-hosted framework that automates the end-to-end job hunt: it searches portals, scores posting fit against your profile, generates tailored LaTeX CVs and cover letters, and coaches interview prep — all driven by Claude Code. It trended as a compelling real-world showcase of Claude Code as a full agentic system for a task everyone relates to. Job seekers who are comfortable with a command line and LaTeX will unlock the most value; the portal connectors currently target the Danish market but the framework is built to be adapted.
repos.llm_api_note: Requires Claude Pro/Max/Team subscription or Anthropic API credits

repos.description: A performance-optimization harness for AI coding agents, with skills, memory, security tooling, and research-first workflows across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and others.
repos.analysis: ECC is a universal harness that installs into AI coding agents — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode — and enriches them with ~70 agents, 311 skills, TDD loops, code-review hooks, persistent memory, and security scanning without changing the underlying agent. Its enormous star count reflects adoption across every major agent platform, and it trended again likely on a new skill pack release. Professional developers who use AI coding assistants daily and want consistent, auditable engineering workflows across projects and teams will find it immediately valuable.
repos.llm_api_note: Runs inside Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or OpenCode — each needs its own access

repos.description: A project to make arbitrary software controllable by AI agents through command-line interfaces, with an accompanying CLI hub.
repos.analysis: CLI-Anything solves the 'tool surface' problem in agentic workflows by generating command-line interfaces for any software — from GIMP and Blender to LibreOffice — so AI agents can control them without brittle GUI automation. CLI-Hub, the companion registry, lets users browse and install community-built CLIs with a single command. It trended on growing demand for expanding what AI coding agents can actually act on; automation engineers, creative-workflow teams, and researchers who need agents to operate domain-specific desktop tools will find it a practical unlock.
repos.llm_api_note: CLI generator runs inside Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex

repos.description: A library of 177+ validated agent skills and 100+ scientific databases for research in biology, chemistry, medicine, and drug discovery.
repos.analysis: A curated collection of 177+ validated agent skills that give AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) structured access to 100+ scientific databases — NCBI, Materials Project, Benchling, and more — across biology, chemistry, medicine, and drug discovery. Trending on growing momentum for AI-assisted scientific research, it offers ready-made, peer-reviewed integrations rather than DIY database wrappers. Computational scientists, bioinformaticians, and research teams who already use an AI coding agent will unlock significant productivity gains without having to build database connectors from scratch.
repos.llm_api_note: Skills for Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex; some databases need separate API keys
